info.name: Ride Hailing Backend
info.description:
Ride Hailing Backend - modular monolith (Spring Boot 3.5 / MySQL 8 / Redis).

## Getting started
1. Set the `baseUrl` variable if the app is not on port 8080.
2. Run **0. Auth** -> the three login requests. Each stores its JWT in a collection
   variable (`riderToken`, `driverToken`, `adminToken`) automatically.
3. Run **2. Drivers -> Update driver location** at least once BEFORE booking.

## Why the location ping matters
A driver is only matchable while a *fresh* GPS position exists in Redis.
`driver.location.ttl.seconds` is 60, so the positions loaded at application
startup expire after a minute and the driver is pruned from the GEO set.
Without a recent ping every booking returns `NO_DRIVER_IN_RADIUS`.

## Demo credentials (development only)
| Account | Password | Role |
|---|---|---|
| admin@ridehailing.com | Admin@123 | ADMIN |
| rahul@ / priya@ / amit@ridehailing.com | User@123 | USER |
| raj.kumar@ / amit.sharma@ / vikram.singh@ / neha.verma@ridehailing.com | Driver@123 | DRIVER |

## City based pricing
Fares depend on the PICKUP location. Seeded zones: DELHI, PUNE, BANGALORE - each mapped to its
own pricing rule. See folder **6. Pricing** for zone management and **9. City pricing demo**
for an end to end proof.

Every response uses the envelope `{ success, data | error, requestId, timestamp }`.

request.description:
Rate limited to 10/minute per rider. The rider is taken from the JWT - the body has no userId.

Flow: rate limit -> idempotency -> validation -> config -> Redis GEO search ->
matching strategy -> atomic driver reservation in MySQL -> ride + pricing snapshot -> audit.

9.1 km hatchback on the seeded rule = 2x10 + 3x8 + 4.102x5 = 64.51, x0.9 = 58.06.

request.description: Changing a rule never alters the fare of an existing ride - every ride stores its own pricing snapshot.

A zone maps a PICKUP point to a pricing rule, so Delhi, Pune and Bengaluru charge different rates with no code change.

Seeded: DELHI (50 km, DELHI_STANDARD), PUNE (30 km, PUNE_STANDARD), BANGALORE (40 km, STANDARD). Outside every zone the global pricing.active.rule applies.

Adding a city is one API call. Create its pricing rule first via POST /pricing/rules if it needs its own rates.

priority breaks overlaps: a small airport zone at priority 200 nested inside a city zone wins automatically.
Redrawing a zone never changes a historical fare - each ride stored its own pricing snapshot and zone code.

item.name: 9. City pricing demo (Delhi)
item.description:
Proves city based pricing end to end.

Seeded drivers are all in Bengaluru, so a Delhi booking would fail with NO_DRIVER_IN_RADIUS before pricing is ever reached - the GEO search runs first. Run these in order to put a driver in Delhi, then book.

Expected: the same 9 km trip costs more in Delhi (min 60, 12/9/6 per km) than in Bengaluru (min 50, 10/8/5 per km).

request.description: Public onboarding. Creates the login account and the driver profile together.
Must run within driver.location.ttl.seconds (60) of the booking, or the driver is pruned as stale.
Pickup falls inside the DELHI zone, so DELHI_STANDARD prices it. Check fare.pricingZoneCode in the response.
